culture.title: Carnegie Museum of Art
culture.description: The art half of the Carnegie in Oakland, with a strong modern collection and the vast Hall of Architecture full of plaster casts.
culture.bonus: Find the Hall of Architecture and look up.

culture.title: The Andy Warhol Museum
culture.description: Seven floors on Pittsburgh's most famous son, the largest museum in North America devoted to a single artist.
culture.bonus: Sit for a screen test in the basement.

culture.title: The Frick Pittsburgh
culture.description: The Gilded Age estate of Henry Clay Frick in Point Breeze, the family mansion, a car and carriage museum and a small art museum across the lawn.
culture.bonus: Take the house tour, then have tea in the café.

culture.title: Nationality Rooms at the Cathedral of Learning
culture.description: Working classrooms inside a 42-storey Gothic tower, each designed by a different immigrant community in the style of its homeland.
culture.bonus: Sit in a room from a country you have never visited.

culture.title: The Mattress Factory
culture.description: A museum of room-sized installation art on the North Side, including permanent James Turrell and Yayoi Kusama rooms.
culture.bonus: Stand in the Kusama mirror room for a full minute.

culture.title: Heinz History Center
culture.description: Six floors of western Pennsylvania history in an old Strip District icehouse, including a sports museum and the original Mister Rogers set.

culture.title: Tour Frank Lloyd Wright's Fallingwater
culture.description: The house built over a waterfall, Frank Lloyd Wright's masterpiece, cantilevered over Bear Run in the Laurel Highlands.
culture.bonus: Walk down to the viewpoint below the falls for the classic angle.

culture.title: Pittsburgh Symphony at Heinz Hall
culture.description: One of America's great orchestras in a restored 1927 movie palace in the downtown Cultural District.
culture.bonus: Dress up more than you think you need to.

social.title: Karaoke at Belvedere's Ultra-Dive
social.description: A proudly scruffy Lawrenceville dive famous for its themed nights, dance parties and a crowd with no shame.
social.bonus: Sing a song everyone knows the chorus to.

social.title: Riverhounds Match at Highmark Stadium
social.description: Pro soccer on the riverbank below Mount Washington, where the downtown skyline is the backdrop to every goal.
social.bonus: Sit with the Steel Army supporters' section.

social.title: Dance Night at Spirit
social.description: A former Moose lodge in Lawrenceville with a pizza counter downstairs and a dance floor upstairs.

social.title: Bowling at Arsenal Lanes
social.description: An old-school upstairs bowling alley in Lawrenceville with cheap beer and a crowd that takes it just seriously enough.
social.bonus: Losing team buys the next round.

social.title: Cocktails at Bar Marco
social.description: A restaurant and cocktail bar inside a converted Strip District firehouse, with a wine cellar in the old basement.

social.title: Live Music at Mr. Smalls Theatre
social.description: A mid-sized concert venue in a converted church just over the river in Millvale, with great sound and a balcony.
social.bonus: Catch the opener. They're often the better band.

social.title: Penguins Game at PPG Paints Arena
social.description: NHL hockey in front of one of the league's most loyal crowds, a short walk from downtown bars.
social.bonus: Get there for warm-ups and watch from the glass.

social.title: Steelers Game at Acrisure Stadium
social.description: Tailgate on the North Shore, then a full stadium waving Terrible Towels by the rivers, Pittsburgh at full volume.
social.bonus: Bring a Terrible Towel and don't stop waving it.

social.title: Rooftop Drinks Downtown
social.description: Order a round at a downtown rooftop bar with the whole skyline lit up around you.
social.bonus: Make a toast to something none of you have done yet this year.

social.title: Trivia Night at Grist House Craft Brewery
social.description: Grab a table in the taproom and battle it out over cold beer at one of Pittsburgh's most-loved weekly trivia nights.
social.bonus: Team up with the table next to you if you're short a player.

social.title: Beer Garden Hangout at Cinderlands Warehouse
social.description: Post up at long communal tables in the Strip District taproom's beer garden with a rotating lineup of small-batch brews.
social.bonus: Order the beer you know the least about on the board.

social.title: Catch a Pirates Game at PNC Park
social.description: Take a seat at what's routinely ranked the most beautiful ballpark in America, skyline rising right over the outfield wall.
social.bonus: Get there early enough to watch the skyline light up during batting practice.

adventure.title: Ski Day at Seven Springs
adventure.description: Western Pennsylvania's biggest ski resort, an hour out of the city, with night skiing and a terrain park.
adventure.bonus: Stay for night skiing under the lights.

adventure.title: Ferncliff Peninsula and Cucumber Falls
adventure.description: A loop around a river peninsula full of fossils and rare plants, then a short walk to a 30-foot waterfall you can stand behind.
adventure.bonus: Wade into the pool at the bottom of Cucumber Falls.

adventure.title: Bike the Three Rivers Heritage Trail Loop
adventure.description: A flat riverside loop crossing the city's bridges past both stadiums and the Point, with the skyline in view the entire way.
adventure.bonus: Cross at least three different bridges.

adventure.title: Mountain Bike Hartwood Acres
adventure.description: Flowy wooded singletrack north of the city, on the grounds of a Tudor-style mansion estate.
adventure.bonus: Finish with a lap on the field in front of the mansion.

adventure.title: Panther Hollow Trail in Schenley Park
adventure.description: A wooded ravine trail through Oakland's big park, dropping down to a quiet lake that feels miles from campus.
adventure.bonus: Finish with the view from Flagstaff Hill.

adventure.title: Raft the Lower Yough at Ohiopyle
adventure.description: Seven miles of class III–IV whitewater on the Youghiogheny River, one of the busiest stretches of whitewater in the East, starting just below Ohiopyle Falls.
adventure.bonus: Swim the Swimmers Rapid if your guide says it's on.

adventure.title: Phantom's Revenge at Kennywood
adventure.description: A century-old amusement park with classic wooden coasters and the Phantom's Revenge, which dives into a ravine at over 80 mph.
adventure.bonus: Ride the Jack Rabbit too. It's been running since 1920.

adventure.title: Lake Loop at North Park
adventure.description: A five-mile paved loop around the county's biggest park lake, with boat rentals and trails running off into the woods.
adventure.bonus: Rent a kayak and paddle the lake after your loop.

adventure.title: Conquer the South Side Slopes Staircases
adventure.description: Climb one of America's densest networks of public staircases, hundreds of steps straight up a hillside neighborhood, for a view most tourists never see.
adventure.bonus: Find and climb the steepest staircase in the neighborhood without stopping to rest.

adventure.title: Run the Eliza Furnace Trail
adventure.description: Log miles along the flat riverside path locals call the Jail Trail, Monongahela River on one side, downtown skyline on the other.
adventure.bonus: Pick a landmark across the river and run until it's directly across from you.

adventure.title: Ride the Duquesne Incline to Mount Washington
adventure.description: Climb the 1877 cable car up the bluff for the single best skyline view of the three rivers meeting downtown.
adventure.bonus: Ride up for sunset and stay until the lights come on downtown.

adventure.title: Bike the Great Allegheny Passage
adventure.description: Roll out from Point State Park onto a flat, riverside rail-trail that eventually stretches all the way to DC.
adventure.bonus: Ride until you hit the first mile marker and text a photo of it to a friend.

adventure.title: Ice Skate at PPG Place
adventure.description: Glide across the outdoor rink ringed by the glass Gothic spires of PPG Place in the heart of downtown.
adventure.bonus: Skate one full lap without holding the rail.

adventure.title: Hike the Fern Hollow Loop in Frick Park
adventure.description: Wind through a wooded ravine trail in one of Pittsburgh's largest and wildest city parks.
adventure.bonus: Spot and name three different tree species along the trail.

foodie.title: Gelato and Pizza at Mercurio's
foodie.description: A Shadyside spot doing Neapolitan pizza from a wood-fired oven and a long case of house-made gelato.

foodie.title: Pierogies at S&D Polish Deli
foodie.description: A small Strip District deli selling homemade pierogies, kielbasa and Polish groceries, Pittsburgh's heritage food done properly.
foodie.bonus: Try a flavour you can't pronounce.

foodie.title: Fish Sandwich at Wholey's
foodie.description: A giant fried-fish sandwich that hangs well off the bun, from the Strip District seafood market with the smiling fish on the sign.
foodie.bonus: Try to finish the whole thing in one sitting.

foodie.title: Burnt Almond Torte at Prantl's
foodie.description: Pittsburgh's most famous cake, layers of sponge and custard buried in a coat of toasted, sugared almonds.
foodie.bonus: Buy a whole one and share it with strangers.

foodie.title: Window-Seat Dinner on Mount Washington
foodie.description: Dinner on top of Mount Washington at Monterey Bay Fish Grotto, where the rivers meet directly beneath the window and the whole skyline lights up.
foodie.bonus: Book the latest window table and stay through the lights coming on.

foodie.title: Hardwood-Grilled Burger at Tessaro's
foodie.description: A dark wood-panelled Bloomfield tavern grilling half-pound burgers over hardwood, often cited as the best in the city.
foodie.bonus: Order it the way the server recommends.

foodie.title: Crepe Pancakes at Pamela's Diner
foodie.description: Thin, crispy-edged pancakes rolled around strawberries and sour cream, at a cash-only diner that has fed presidents.
foodie.bonus: Get the strawberry hotcakes, no substitutions.

foodie.title: Plant-Based Polish at Apteka
foodie.description: A Bloomfield restaurant doing fully vegan Central and Eastern European food with national acclaim, a pierogi plate that changes minds.
foodie.bonus: Order one dish you'd normally assume needs meat.

foodie.title: Pint and Pretzel at Church Brew Works
foodie.description: Drink a house-brewed lager beneath stained glass and vaulted ceilings inside an actual converted 19th-century church.
foodie.bonus: Sit in what used to be a pew and order the sampler flight.

foodie.title: Saturday Morning Strip District Market Crawl
foodie.description: Weave through open-air stalls, spice shops, and Italian delis in the neighborhood that built Pittsburgh's food scene.
foodie.bonus: Buy one ingredient you've never cooked with before.

foodie.title: Original Sandwich at Primanti Bros
foodie.description: Order the classic at the Strip District original, fries and coleslaw piled right inside the sandwich, no substitutions.
foodie.bonus: Eat it standing up at the counter like a local.

foodie.title: Chef's Counter Dinner at Butcher and the Rye
foodie.description: Book the counter for a whiskey-paired tasting menu at one of downtown Pittsburgh's most acclaimed kitchens.
foodie.bonus: Let the bartender pick your whiskey pour, no menu required.

chill.title: Espresso at La Prima
chill.description: An Italian espresso bar in the Strip where the old-timers play cards at the back tables and the cappuccino is a proper one.
chill.bonus: Drink it standing up at the bar, Italian-style.

chill.title: Browse Caliban Book Shop
chill.description: An antiquarian and used bookshop on Craig Street stacked floor to ceiling with literature, art books and first editions.
chill.bonus: Buy something from the rare-books shelf under $20.

chill.title: Gateway Clipper River Cruise
chill.description: A sightseeing cruise on all three rivers from Station Square, passing under the bridges with the skyline sliding by.
chill.bonus: Stand on the top deck as you pass the Point.

chill.title: Walled Garden at Mellon Park
chill.description: A sunken formal garden hidden behind stone walls in Shadyside, left over from a demolished mansion.
chill.bonus: Bring a book and read one chapter on the lawn.

chill.title: Sunset at the West End Overlook
chill.description: A quieter alternative to Mount Washington, a hilltop park looking straight up the Ohio River into downtown.
chill.bonus: Stay until every bridge is lit.

chill.title: Wander Allegheny Cemetery
chill.description: A 300-acre Victorian garden cemetery in Lawrenceville, full of hilltop monuments, old trees and total quiet.

chill.title: Sunset at the Point State Park Fountain
chill.description: Watch the fountain arc over the exact spot where the Allegheny and Monongahela become the Ohio River.
chill.bonus: Watch until the three rivers actually disappear into one color in the fading light.

chill.title: Wander Phipps Conservatory and Botanical Gardens
chill.description: Drift through glasshouse rooms of orchids, bonsai, and seasonal flower shows in one of the country's oldest conservatories.
chill.bonus: Find the one room that smells the best and stay there an extra five minutes.

chill.title: Sit with the Dinosaurs at Carnegie Museum of Natural History
chill.description: Spend a slow afternoon under full-scale dinosaur skeletons in one of the largest natural history collections in the country.
chill.bonus: Pick your favorite skeleton and learn one fact about it before you leave.

chill.title: Explore Randyland
chill.description: Step inside a free, wildly painted folk-art house and yard on the Northside that turns an entire block into a mural.
chill.bonus: Find the founder Randy if he's around and say hello.

8ball.title: Cross a Bridge You've Never Crossed
8ball.description: The city of bridges has more than 400 of them. Pick one you've never crossed on foot, walk to the far side, and spend the afternoon in whatever neighbourhood you land in.
8ball.bonus: Eat at the first place you pass that has no sign.

8ball.title: Take a Staircase You've Never Climbed
8ball.description: Pittsburgh has more public staircases than any city in the country. Pick one you've never taken, climb it, and go into the first bar or café at the top.
